reviews.review: Better than I expected it to be, but fails even on it's own merits. Constant influxes of tedious side gigs and menial busywork that forces constant re-exploration of planets and poi that you've already been to. Has boring combat, weak exploration, and weak dialogue. The expanded paragon/renegade system is KIND OF interesting? But the story is lame, the lore is lame, the characters feel vapid and artificial, and the game is visually generic if not outwardly ugly at certain points. At times this game feels like it's trying to hit all the hallmarks of classic AAA slop like its ticking off boxes on a checklist. Lifeless, boring, corporate, gentrified, and at no point does it ever feel like Mass Effect. Avoid avoid avoid.

Not a bad mass effect games, and before bioware really drops in quality in the future, but definitely a very stripped down and missing some bones here and there. Definitely worth playing if a mass effect fan, but it will undoubtedly be the worse mass effect in the series so far.

Played this game on it's own merits, doing the hardcore mode difficulty ( did this with the original trilogy completely; not machoistic enough for Insanity lol) and giving up after doing at most a couple of explorable planets. Total hours: 27.2. Take this as someone who no longer had patience to play this, and not as a real review. Main gripes?

 The gameplay loop is tedious, while the combat is at least enjoyable, but not enough for me to look past everything. Scan some stuff here, drop a pod there, to expand, but most areas will be gated off on certain wide scale planets, until you progress in the game. At least in ME1, when you explored a planet, no matter how generic or barren it looked, you certainly had the means to explore it fully, and encouraged to do so. The "gates" put in place to keep you from going forward in Andromeda, don't make it clear what could be needed to continue at times. The obvious of course, involves a Vault story wise, but outside of that, it's just a gate for you to go back to later for the sake of extending gameplay time by needing some upgrade or what not.

  The checkpoint system is perhaps the most egregious part of this game, and moments where you should be able to save, is dictated by whether that area is safe enough to do so, while forcing you to go through areas like a vault without saving for some gods forsaken reason. Wanted to explore, but made a mistake and got yourself killed? Better pray that checkpoint was at a moment where you didn't want to fight all of those enemies again. There are also cases like this when fighting overworld bosses, which have scripted phases that may require you to go to a specific spot. Thinking of saving? Can't! Spent a minute getting it's health down to trigger the next phase transition, but died to something stupid? Oh wait, checkpoint was a few minutes ago, and reloading just sets you at the first phase. Time to do that again!

Those grievances aside,  I will say that this is by far in a much better state than it originally was, since it's release! So no awkward faces and such (much), and crashes were extremely few if non existent. Story wise, from what I experienced after I finished Havarl (and went to one of the Angara worlds), it's passable, but certainly nothing compared to the original trilogy, even if you had gripes about 2 & 3. At most the urgency of finding necessary planets to colonize was a nice motivator, and actually exploring and learning about the Golden Worlds was at least engaging to some extent. Banter between your teammates was fine, and most of them do have some overall entertaining things to say, but your ragtag Pathfinder crew is about as deep as a puddle, and just as stimulating as eating a bowl of cereal after an 8 hour shift. You see the potential for them to be more interesting, but they're so basic at times, that I can't help but see them as nothing more than other NPCs on the station. I will say the "Horde Mode" was at least fun, when I did play it back on Origin (when that used to be a thing), and likely would be more fun the further I went into playing Andromeda, but I can't bring myself to continue. Spending another 20 hours or more on this game, would be better off on something more worthwhile.

I'm a massive Mass Effect fan and while this game was rough at launch, now that it's been fixed it's really not as bad as some people say it is. Does it hold up to the trilogy? Not exactly, it's a completely different stories with completely different goals and mechanics, so you have to understand that going in. Some of the quests can be a bit repetitive but I thought it was cool exploring more things about the universe and like usual, the companions were really amazing. I'll never forgive them for shafting us of real turian romance, but overall I would give it a 7.5/10.
It might not be as great as original trilogy but it is much better when you give it a chance to stand on its two legs
